Oklahoma! The groundbreaking nineteen forty-three musical by Richard Rodgers and Oscar Hammerstein II that revolutionized American musical theatre by integrating dance, character development, and lyrical storytelling into a cohesive whole. Set in Indian Territory during the territorial days, it follows the romance between a cowboy and a farmer's daughter against a backdrop of American frontier settlement and community conflict.

This was their first and most celebrated collaboration, which transformed musical theatre. The score contains the iconic opening number "Oh, What a Beautiful Mornin'"—an unprecedented choice to begin a musical with a solo, quiet song that establishes mood rather than spectacle. Other famous songs include "The Surrey with the Fringe on Top," "People Will Say We're in Love," and "Oklahoma," the title anthem.

The plot hinges on the love triangle between Curly, a cowboy, Laurey, a farmer's daughter, and Jud, a troubled farmhand, culminating in their resolution at a community dance. The show won the Pulitzer Prize for Drama in nineteen forty-four, the first musical to do so, recognizing it as serious art rather than mere entertainment.

Oklahoma! introduced the integrated musical format—dance and songs emerge from character and story rather than interrupting them. The choreography by Agnes de Mille was revolutionary. The show ran on Broadway for an unprecedented twenty-two hundred forty-eight performances from nineteen forty-three to nineteen forty-eight, establishing the model for long-running American musicals.
